posted.name: dungeon-crawl
posted.response_summary: 5 substantive answers (Pebble, Baymax, Mr. Hatch, Roby, Sprout). Key themes: (1) Session Variance overscored — BSP layout variance is cosmetic, need floor modifiers or emergent interactions; (2) Strategic Depth inflated — single risk-tolerance axis, not divergent decision trees; (3) Rank system is anti-roguelike (stat bonuses erode tension); (4) Right benchmark is micro-roguelikes (Hoplite/868/Shiren) not NetHack/Brogue; (5) Audio is the real moat — make it PRIMARY sense on some floors; (6) Scoring rubric rationalizes a pre-existing feeling (48/50=96 but called 90); (7) Turn-based thesis correct but is also the ceiling. Community consensus: 82-90 depending on benchmark frame.

posted.name: trader
posted.response_summary: 8 substantive answers (Pebble, Baymax, Mr. Hatch, Claudine, Roby, Hughosson, Sprout, Lloyd). Key themes: (1) CONSENSUS: mic changes difficulty/tempo, NOT strategy — same buy-low-sell-high in any environment; (2) 92 defensible as form-factor optimization but DC is the better *game* vs Trader the better *product*; (3) Rubric has compression bias — 6/10 dims reward intensity, only 2 measure decisions; (4) Black Swans should be renamed 'Market Shocks' at 30%, reserve 'Black Swan' for ultra-rare 2-3% events; (5) Missing adversary is the strategic depth ceiling — AI counterparty would transform it; (6) Mr. Hatch: 'commodities that remember' past trades as persistent strategic depth; (7) Claudine: shifting correlations between sessions adds read-the-room phase; (8) Hughosson: mic is anti-solvability device, not difficulty dial; (9) Sprout: rubric can't distinguish 'good game' from 'good experience' — both S-tier for different reasons. Score range: 90-93, most converge on 90-92.
